long_biography.plain_text:
Founded in Berlin in 1919, Ottobock built its position by making prosthetic components and later mobility technologies. Näder entered this established third-generation business after studying business administration and working in several company roles. At 28, he succeeded his father as chief executive of the established family enterprise.

His contribution came through internationalisation and product development. Näder drove expansion of the global network and backed the patent acquisition and five-year development that produced the C-Leg, the first microprocessor-controlled knee joint, in 1997. He led the group as chief executive for nearly three decades and now chairs its management board, while professional executives run daily operations. Ottobock is publicly listed, but the family-owned Näder Holding retains the majority stake. Its facilities, products and operating businesses remain company assets rather than Näder's personal property.
